2: 
3: Eko; 21 September 2026, Brisbane. Authorised by Ash's attached Compass continuation and existing R3 commission. This contract does not claim formal blueprint promotion or programme completion. Existing runtime and validation rules are not waived.
4: 
5: ## Purpose and finite exit
6: 
7: Classification: existing frontend lint acceptance gate, not a causal prerequisite to all memory design. The present codegen file contributes 104 of 122 lint errors. Exit this slice when the actual generation pipeline reproducibly emits the same runtime classes without explicit-any, affected consumers pass their regression suite, deliberate-break controls are detected, and independent review reproduces the evidence. Return to the recorded product dependencies rather than expand into unrelated repairs. The other 18 handwritten errors, 11 warnings, Keychain/root/package obligations remain visible and are not waived.
8: 
9: ## Source and design decision
10: 
11: `app/ui/ui.go:42` invokes tscriptify over responses/types.go. The module pins typescriptify-golang-structs v0.2.0; fresh execution reproduces gotypes.gen.ts byte-for-byte (SHA256 49052e66cbd7e279e7bc2abd0270df4f8746fb1545e0e8d486deb51cbf791154). The pinned generator hardcodes constructor/helper any, so configuration alone does not solve this. There are 35 classes and 16 conversion helpers. useChats.ts invokes generated constructors repeatedly; interfaces alone would remove runtime behaviour.
12: 
13: Proposed owning process: a small Node generation command runs the existing pinned Go generator into a fresh temporary file, applies an AST-checked annotation transform using the already installed TypeScript compiler, verifies identical emitted JavaScript under the project compiler options, and atomically replaces only the generated target after all checks succeed. The normal go:generate directive points to this command. No module-cache edits, new package/version, runtime helper, alternate model classes or hand edits of generated output.
14: 
15: Constructor inputs and conversion intermediates become unknown, not a renamed any. Assertions occur at the pre-existing unchecked materialisation boundary and are derived from each generated property's declared type. Public Go interface-valued JSON fields become a recursive JSONValue union (string, number, boolean, null, JSON arrays and objects). This describes serialized JSON; it is NOT a runtime validator and does not reject or repair malformed JavaScript inputs. No claim of input-validation safety is earned by this annotation repair. Existing Go producer behaviour, coercion, optional-field handling and error paths stay unchanged. In particular this work does not redesign time.Time conversion or the byte-array/raw-JSON wire contracts.
16: 
17: Strongest objection: an annotation adapter can drift from its upstream emitter or turn unsafe assertions into a false validation claim. Mitigations: version-pinned raw generator, reject unsupported AST/template shapes, compare emitted JavaScript before writing, retain the explicit unchecked-boundary statement, and executable regeneration/consumer tests. Copying the entire upstream generator to change its templates would add a maintained fork; replacing classes with interfaces breaks live consumers. Disabling lint or wrapping any in an alias is rejected.
18: 
19: ## Requirements
20: 
21: G-01. Use the same Go source-model discovery and pinned generator, without a separately maintained list of model fields/classes. Running normal generation twice produces identical generated bytes; --check detects stale output without modifying it.
22: G-02. Retain all runtime class names, constructors, nested object/array/map conversion, Date transforms, primitive values, absent/null handling and malformed-JSON exceptions. Generated JavaScript must be byte-identical to raw upstream emission using the recorded project options. No new runtime code or imports in generated models.
23: G-03. Emit no explicit-any syntax. Typecheck all affected existing application consumers; lint has zero findings in the generated target and no new findings elsewhere. Remaining baseline debt is enumerated separately.
24: G-04. Generation failures, unsupported shapes, emission mismatch and --check drift leave the existing output unchanged and return a failing child exit. Never truncate the target before verification. Temporary material is scoped and regenerable; retain evidence under the existing task directory.
25: G-05. Default frontend tests cover real generated constructors, contrasting values, nested conversions and actual renderer consumption without replacing the generated classes or renderer. Dedicated generation tests cover the actual CLI and TypeScript annotation logic; keep ordinary frontend tests runnable without a Go installation. Required generation verification is an explicit candidate-acceptance command documented with the generator.
26: G-06. Freeze candidate and permanent tests in a local commit before T-05. Run clean–broken–clean controls in isolated copies: bypass annotation generation (lint must fail); drop nested conversion (consumer assertion must fail after compilation); corrupt a delivered value (contrasting-input assertion must fail after compilation). Show the fault reached its expected assertion. A missing dependency, collection failure or type error does not qualify as behavioural detection.
27: G-07. Capture all commands, full stdout/stderr, true exits, source/config/dependency identities and discovered/completed cases. Run the complete established frontend suite, project typecheck, full lint comparison and production frontend build. Independently reproduce required acceptance and controls with the selected DeepSeek judge before a passing bounded review.
28: 
29: ## Scope and recovery
30: 
31: Expected owned changes: generator command/annotation module and tests; normal go:generate invocation; generated model output; required acceptance documentation. No production Go model/handler, store, renderer, dependency lock or lint-policy change is intended. An unexpected need to change runtime semantics returns to this contract before implementation.
32: 
33: The committed task branch and source baseline provide recovery for code; generated output is independently reproducible from retained Go source and pinned dependencies. Do not touch live conversations, Keychain, installations, global settings, other worktrees or unrelated processes. Main integration remains gated separately.
34: 
35: ## Pre-code refinement R2 — authoritative over the proposed adapter details above
36: 
37: Public type ownership stays in Go. Add only ts_type metadata: app/store/store.go ToolFunction.Result uses JSONValue; app/ui/responses/types.go ChatEvent.ToolResultData, ChatEvent.ToolState and ChatRequest.Think use JSONValue; ChatEvent.ApprovalArgs uses {[key: string]: JSONValue}. Preserve every json tag and all executable Go statements. The existing Go generator emits these annotations itself. The adapter MUST NOT replace any public property types; it rejects a public AnyKeyword, including one in a generic or ts_type override, and requires a deliberate Go-source contract instead. It provides the JSONValue alias once, rejecting a declaration/name collision. This replaces the prototype's public-type inference and avoids a shadow Go-type map.
38: 
39: The transform is a pure function of raw generator bytes, the checked transform source and the installed/pinned TypeScript API. Only constructor parameter annotations, convertValues parameter/return annotations, and erased assertions on constructor reads/assignments and helper object indexing may change. All edits are bounded by parsed AST ranges; zero string searches choose edit positions. Reject overlapping ranges and unsupported constructor statements, transform expressions, members and top-level declarations. Locate a guarded Date transform's left operand via its AST, not the first textual &&. Identical JavaScript is a separate invariant checked on every generation, not inferred from the allowed edit list.
40: 
41: Emission comparison uses TypeScript Program.emit for the generated module with parsed tsconfig.app.json options, overriding noEmit to false and using identical source-map/comment settings for both arms. Preserve the real config hash and option overrides. This is compiler equivalence, not the Vite/browser path. Actual tsc -b --force, npm test -- --run, npm run lint and npm run build remain required acceptance commands. CORRECTION: the first Program comparison failed with TS5096 because allowImportingTsExtensions requires noEmit. The R2 draft prematurely claimed success before its output was read. That claim is withdrawn; the original failure is retained in program-compare.stderr. For this import-free generated module, disable allowImportingTsExtensions only in the comparison options, together with noEmit=false; record the exact options and actual result in program-compare-r2.stdout. This is not a change to tsconfig or the real build.
42: 
43: Normal entry: app/ui/ui.go's generation directive invokes node ./app/codegen/generate.mjs. package.json exposes generate:types, check:types (--check), and test:codegen. The dedicated test:codegen command uses Node's installed standard-library test runner on codegen/generate.checks.mjs, covering the Node CLI including real Go generation. It is a required codegen-change acceptance command, NOT part of the ordinary frontend npm test and not a claim of newly installed CI enforcement. Default Vitest gains generated-model/real-renderer regression tests without a Go prerequisite.
44: 
45: --check regenerates from live Go model sources into owned scratch, runs the same annotation transform and emission guard, and byte-compares the final transformed output with the existing target. Mismatch is non-zero and never writes the target. Normal generation also writes only after all upstream/transform/emission checks, using a same-directory temporary file and atomic rename. Failed generation and unsupported templates preserve the old target. The command may accept --output for an explicit alternative target, primarily to make the actual CLI testable without touching the committed file. No static cached candidate can substitute for a fresh generation.
46: 
47: T-05 edits to generated JavaScript/TypeScript are allowed ONLY in isolated fault copies. The prohibition on hand patching generated output governs the accepted production pipeline, not deliberate-break fixtures. This is consistent with the attached prompt and Method04 T-05. The nested-copy fault replaces Chat.messages conversion with an empty typed array; the delivered-value fault replaces Message.content with a fixed string. Both must compile and fail the unchanged default consumer tests for their intended reason. A bypass-annotation control writes raw upstream output in an isolated copy and must fail the explicit-any check/linter while still compiling. No fault touches the owned candidate or main.
48: 
49: Test the public-type refusal, collision refusal, deterministic transform, unsupported shape refusal, actual Go regeneration twice, --check success/stale/no-write, failing Go subprocess/no-write, and default generated constructor/value/renderer behaviour. There is no new general JSON validation promise. Existing Time, byte-array and raw-JSON conversion quirks are explicitly NOT redefined or blessed as correct by these tests.
50: 
51: R2 source scope includes the two Go metadata owners plus the generation directive, Node command/transform/test, generated output, package commands, frontend regression test and generator documentation. No Go handler algorithm, persisted format, dependency version, lint rule, renderer logic, Keychain or installation is changed.
52: 
53: ## Final design clarifications R3
54: 
55: Both normal generation and --check call one shared verification function with the same raw generation, source inputs, type transform and compiler guard. The only mode difference is the final action: byte comparison or atomic replacement. The target is untouched until that action. --output selects the sole target for the invocation under the identical checks; using a distinct output leaves the committed target unchanged.
56: 
57: The Program comparison rejects any parse/pre-emit/emit diagnostic, emitSkipped or missing JavaScript output. The parsed project options and comparison-only overrides are retained explicitly. TypeScript's allowImportingTsExtensions must be false when emitting JavaScript; this is safe for the import-free generated module and is not a tsconfig modification. Raw and refined arms receive identical options.
58: 
59: The JSONValue alias is a fixed adapter-owned recursive JSON union, independent of Go metadata and using no any or other helper alias. A raw declaration that shadows it is rejected. Every raw public property containing any is rejected, never inferred. The five deliberate Go ts_type annotations listed in R2 are the public type decisions; other source additions must supply their own correct types.
60: 
61: G-02 guards accepted generation only. Deliberately broken isolated T-05 copies are not accepted candidates and do not have to satisfy the equality invariant they are used to challenge. No mutant enters the owned worktree or normal output.
62: 
63: The comparison baseline for lint and source is baseline/lint.json and git-preflight.json in this continuation's evidence directory (122 errors,11 warnings at b880138b). New whole-file warning findings are not waived. The twice-run generation check includes the entire Go metadata discovery/extraction, not merely rerunning the annotation function."}
